It took all day, but our talented judge team and event staff went through 2095 Decklists to find out which Decks Duelists are using this weekend. They categorized each Deck by “Main Type” and, if applicable, “Sub Types”; but for the purposes of this article and the simplification of the statistics involved, we’ll focus on the “Main Type” used by this weekend’s competitors.
Here’s how many of each “Main Type” was entered into this weekend’s North America WCQ:

Salamangreat: 421 Duelists (approximately 20%)
Danger: 420 Duelists (approximately 20%)
Sky Striker: 282 Duelists (approximately 13%)
Orcust: 240 Duelists (approximately 11%)
True Draco: 96 Duelists (approximately 5%)
Altergeist: 79 Duelists (approximately 4%)
Thunder Dragon: 64 Duelists (approximately 3%)
Subterror: 50 Duelists (approximately 2%)
Phantom Knight: 49 Duelists (approximately 2%)
Trickstar: 42 Duelists (approximately 2%)
Pendulum Endymion: 38 Duelists (approximately 2%)
Dinosaur: 30 Duelists (approximately 1%)
Cyber Dragon: 28 Duelists (approximately 1%)
Mekk-Knight: 26 Duelists (approximately 1%)

Keep in mind that each Deck could only be categorized by one “Main Type”, even though many Decks used by this weekend’s Duelists use several different strategies that are integral to the success of their Deck. Nevertheless, the rough numbers shown above give you an approximation of what Decks Duelists are using at this highest level of competitive play. other types of Decks with less than 1% of representation (20 or fewer Duelists) in the tournament, including Burn Decks, Train Decks, Paleozoic Decks, SPYRAL Decks, Infernoid Decks, Gem-Knight Decks, Lunalight Decks, and

While the World Championship Qualifier brings together Duelists who qualified over the last year, the WCQ also brings together fans of the Yu-Gi-Oh! series!
We found Bandit Keith – well, really Shawn Patton from Pittsburgh – in the crowd at the WCQ alongside Joey Wheeler – actually Alexis, also from Pittsburgh at the 2019 North America WCQ.
They didn’t play in the WCQ itself as neither of them secured an invite. Alexis doesn’t play competitively, and Shawn has a Bandit Keith-themed Machine Deck, ready to take on all challengers!
Shawn and Alexis can be seen at Tekko, a local anime convention and usually run a Yu-Gi-Oh! trivia panel.

Both Shawn and Alexis have been involved in the game since the beginning. Shawn also judged at all levels of tournaments from 2004 to 2014, going all the way up to Yu-Gi-Oh! Championship Series and Canadian National Championships! “When Shawn texted me and said ‘do you wanna go to the WCQ in town’ I said ‘yeah!’ I looked up if any voice actors were gonna be there and I saw that Wayne Grayson was going to be there” which was convenient because Alexis is known for her Joey cosplay. “I don’t have a Deck but I might play a Sealed tournament with [Shawn].”

used their Sky Striker and Danger! Thunder Dragon Decks to take victory and earn an invitation to the World Championship before today’s event even begins. Despite the fact that they’ve already won the most coveted prize of the weekend – that elusive invitation to compete on the global level – both of them are continuing to put their skills to the test by participating in the WCQ.

are here at the 2019 Dragon Duel World Championship Qualifier from London, Ontario, Canada. Jonathan’s been playing for 2 years and he got his invite for the Dragon Duel WCQ from the Dragon Duel at the Yu-Gi-Oh Championship Series at Niagara Falls in 2018.

“I’m highly involved and invested in the game”, says Melissa. “Johnathan plays every Tuesday, we go right after school and have dinner in a plaza. He pre-plays with the guys and plays until 9:30 to 10:00pm every week, even on a school night! Even on weeks he’s with his father, I still take him.”

The Yu-Gi-Oh! TRADING CARD GAME can encourage players to develop skills needed to play a TCG. But there’s also other lessons that can be learned from playing the game. “He loves chess, and chess is all strategy, there’s no luck. With Yu-Gi-Oh, there’s strategy and luck, and you can’t predict and control everything, and luck is a part of life. In Yu-Gi-Oh, you can’t control everything, so how do you regroup when the opponent plays a card that makes you lose? That’s just part of the game.” In addition to all that, Jonathan’s also learned some economic lessons from the game. “He’ll do
from flyers to chores to earn money to get cards. It teaches him the value of work to earn something that’s of value to you.

Jonathan loves going to premiere events because “there’s a wow factor”, says Melissa. “It’s kids from all over, all races and nationalities for a common love. For the most part, it’s a happy activity celebrating the love of the cards. For the most part, everyone’s happy.”

Kris’s older brothers also play the TCG, and Mark plays with them at home and brings them to Game On, a Konami Official Tournament Store in Prescott, Arizona for their tournaments.

Duel Links is now a part of Public Events at YCS and WCQ events! This weekend, Duelists were able to participate in 8-player tournaments with the chance to win exclusive Duel Links pins. The latest Duel Links Public Event at the 2019 North America WCQ just finished. Check out the first and second place Duelists, and take a look at the strategies they used in their path to triumph!

The rules of the tournament were simple: There were 8 Duelists competing, each using their own Duel Links account. Each round was played as a Best-of-Three Match, and all Duelists could use whichever cards, characters, and skills they wanted to use in each Duel. In essence, everything in a Duelist’s account was that Duelist’s “Side Deck”. As a result, successful Duelists in the tournament were constantly switching Decks, characters, and skills, between Duels and between Rounds, in order to keep their opponents guessing about what was in store.
James Davis was the ultimate winner in the latest Duel Links tournament.

Davis mostly used his Subterror Deck with Lumis and Umbra’s “Masked Tribute” skill in the tournament, but he also switched into his Blue-Eyes Deck with the “Beatdown” skill and Ancient Gear Deck with the “Middle Age Mechs” skill between Duels. Mostly using his Subterror Deck, he managed to win the tournament and take home the 1
Place Lion Pin, representing the “King of Games” rank in Duel Links. Throughout the tournament, Davis encountered a variety of Decks, including Subterrors, Red-Eyes, and Neos.
